subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

**Hardly I had entered** the room when the phone rang.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an error in its structure, specifically in the placement of the auxiliary verb "had" and the subject "I."
 
• In sentences with "hardly" followed by a past perfect tense, the auxiliary verb "had" must precede the subject.
 
• The correct structure is "Hardly had I entered" to ensure grammatical accuracy and proper sentence construction.
 
• Thus, the bold part needs to be replaced with **Option 1: Hardly had I entered**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Hardly had I entered the room when the phone rang."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Hardly was I entering** – This option is incorrect as it uses the past continuous tense, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: I had hardly entered** – This option changes the structure and meaning of the sentence, making it less precise.
 
• **Option 4: I hardly had entered** – This option incorrectly places "hardly" before "had," which disrupts the intended meaning.
